clue.text: See what's in store for an outsider

definitions.text: See what's in store for an outsider

parts.note: surface reading: foresee what the future holds for someone shut out
setter's reading: look at goods in a shop while standing outside it, without buying

explanation.surface: A prophecy about the fate awaiting someone who never fits in.
explanation.walkthrough: 'In store' looks like 'coming up in the future', but it means literally inside a shop.
explanation.definitionFit: To window-shop is to browse displays through the glass from the street, standing outside the shop.

clue.text: Immersing page in water produced tears

indicators.note: immersing something puts it right inside, so one piece is surrounded by the other

parts.note: wet means watery, soaked with water
P is the abbreviation for page

explanation.surface: Someone cried while dunking a sheet of paper.
explanation.walkthrough: P goes inside WET to make WEPT.
explanation.definitionFit: Wept is the past tense of weep, to cry, so it means shed or produced tears.

clue.text: He allowed nothing odd on his vessel

definitions.text: He allowed nothing odd on his vessel

parts.note: surface reading: a strict captain who tolerated nothing strange aboard

parts.words: He allowed nothing odd on his vessel
parts.note: setter's reading: animals came aboard two by two, so nothing in an odd number

explanation.walkthrough: 'Odd' seems to mean strange, but it is odd as opposed to even: the beasts boarded in pairs.
explanation.definitionFit: In Genesis this patriarch built the ark and took the animals aboard in pairs before the flood.

clue.text: Potter's work men up in a shop ordered

indicators.note: putting things in order rearranges them, so the letters are set out anew

parts.note: every letter of these words is used

explanation.surface: A potter's pieces being ordered up by men in a shop.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Potter' looks like a maker of pots, but it is the writer Stephen Potter, whose humorous 1952 book was titled One-Upmanship.
explanation.definitionFit: One-Upmanship was a book written by Stephen Potter, so it is literally a work by that author.

clue.text: Carefully approach second speech

parts.note: S is the abbreviation for second
a talk is a speech given to an audience

explanation.surface: Cautiously coming forward to give a second address.
explanation.definitionFit: To stalk prey is to creep up on it stealthily, so it means approaching with great care.

clue.text: Submission to live on island in stormy ocean

indicators.note: one thing in another sits inside it, so it is enclosed
a stormy sea is churned up, so its letters are thrown into a new order

parts.note: taken as written before rearranging

indicators.note: one piece placed on another is joined to it, end to end

parts.note: to be is to live, to exist
Is. is the abbreviation for island

explanation.surface: Someone resigned to living on an island amid a raging sea.
explanation.walkthrough: The rearranged sea splits after its first letter to wrap around the living-on-island pair.
explanation.definitionFit: Obeisance is a bow or gesture of deference, showing respectful submission to a superior.

clue.text: Characters in front of queue, say, looking down on others

parts.note: the run of alphabet letters that come before Q, read as A to P
queue sounds like the letter Q, which is where the run of letters stops

explanation.surface: People at the head of a queue gazing down on the rest of the line.
explanation.walkthrough: The letters of the alphabet in front of Q are A to P, so 'A TO P' is read straight into the grid as ATOP.
explanation.definitionFit: Something atop another thing sits on top of it, so it is above and looking down on the rest.

clue.text: Many in parties animated with it?

definitions.text: Many in parties animated with it?

indicators.note: animated means set in lively motion, so the letters are stirred into a new order

parts.note: M is the Roman numeral for a thousand, so many
taken as written
taken as written

explanation.surface: Wondering whether many people at parties are livened up by this.
explanation.walkthrough: The whole clue doubles as the definition: members of a side are fired up by this shared feeling. M for a thousand is a Roman numeral.
explanation.definitionFit: Team spirit is the shared enthusiasm and loyalty that energises members of a group or side.

clue.text: Long nettle leaf

parts.note: to long for is to pine for
to nettle or needle someone is to irritate them

explanation.surface: A long leaf from a stinging nettle plant.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Long' and 'nettle' look like a description of a plant, but both are verbs.
explanation.definitionFit: The thin, sharp needles of a conifer are its leaves, adapted to save water.

clue.text: As mediator, 'e is received by leader of race

indicators.note: something received is taken inside, so one piece goes within the other

parts.note: a pacemaker leads a race to set the speed for the field
the dropped-aitch 'e is just the letter E

explanation.surface: A cockney 'he' acts as mediator, welcomed by the front-runner of a race.
explanation.walkthrough: E goes inside PACEMAKER, after the A, giving PEACEMAKER.
explanation.definitionFit: A peacemaker settles disputes between quarrelling sides, which is exactly the job of a mediator.

clue.text: Noticed new cut

parts.note: saw is the past tense of see, to notice
N is the standard abbreviation for new

explanation.surface: Someone spotted a fresh haircut.
explanation.definitionFit: Sawn is the past participle of saw, so timber that has been sawn has been cut through.

clue.text: Top sportsman as provider of music

definitions.meaning: first meaning, read playfully: a player who sets records
second meaning: a turntable machine that plays discs

explanation.surface: A star athlete who doubles as a source of music.
explanation.walkthrough: The first sense is a pun: a sportsman who breaks records could be called a record player.
explanation.definitionFit: A record player is a gramophone that spins vinyl discs to play recorded songs.

clue.text: Representative steps on ladder for each boy

parts.note: the rungs of a ladder are also called spokes
per means for each, as in miles per hour
a son is a boy

explanation.surface: A rule handing out a fixed number of ladder rungs to every boy.
explanation.definitionFit: A spokesperson speaks on behalf of an organisation, acting as its official representative to the public.

clue.text: School subject

definitions.meaning: first meaning, a verb: to train or correct
second meaning, a noun: a branch of learning

explanation.walkthrough: It reads as 'a school subject', but the two words are separate meanings, the first a verb.
explanation.definitionFit: To discipline is to train someone in obedience, and a discipline is also an academic field of study.

clue.text: 'e isn't involved with water!

indicators.note: things involved with each other are tangled together, so the letters get mixed up

parts.note: the letters of these words, apostrophe dropped
taken as written

explanation.surface: A cockney insists some fellow has nothing to do with water.
explanation.walkthrough: The whole clue also defines the answer: someone who samples wine for a living has no dealings with water.
explanation.definitionFit: A wine-taster samples vintages professionally, so their business is with wine rather than plain water.

clue.text: Copy a restrictive rule, except for initial line

indicators.note: except for means leaving something out, so a letter is taken away

parts.note: a limitation is a rule that restricts what may be done
L is the abbreviation for line, and here it is the first letter

explanation.surface: An instruction to reproduce a regulation, leaving out its opening line.
explanation.walkthrough: LIMITATION loses its first letter L to leave IMITATION.
explanation.definitionFit: An imitation is a reproduction made to resemble an original, so it is a copy.

clue.text: Put together a small contract, for example, with speed

parts.note: in bridge, one no-trump, written 1NT, is a low bid; read as letters it is INT
e.g. is the abbreviation for for example
rate means speed, as in a rate of knots

explanation.surface: Drawing up a minor business deal in a hurry.
explanation.walkthrough: A contract in the card game bridge is the bid a side must make; 1NT is the smallest common one, and the digit 1 stands for I.
explanation.definitionFit: To integrate parts is to combine them into a whole, which is putting them together.

clue.text: Provide a view round wood

parts.note: O is round in shape
pine is a kind of wood

explanation.surface: Offering scenery that looks out around a forest.
explanation.walkthrough: 'View' suggests scenery, but here it means an opinion.
explanation.definitionFit: To opine is to state one's opinion, which is to give a view on a matter.

clue.text: Game in which county quickly succeeded

parts.note: Ches. is the short form of Cheshire, an English county, written quickly
s. is the abbreviation for succeeded, used in family histories

explanation.surface: A sport at which one county won fast.
explanation.walkthrough: Cheshire is a county in north-west England; 'quickly' asks for its abbreviation.
explanation.definitionFit: Chess is a board game for two players moving pieces such as kings and pawns.

clue.text: Routine start of term — study philosopher and economist

indicators.note: the start of a word is its opening letter, so only that letter is kept

parts.note: the opening letter of term
to read a subject is to study it at university
John Stuart Mill was both a philosopher and an economist

explanation.surface: A student's start-of-term routine: reading philosophy and economics.
explanation.definitionFit: A treadmill is figuratively a tedious, repetitive routine one cannot escape, like walking a machine that goes nowhere.

clue.text: Pitch for performing a nocturne?

parts.note: a musician performing a piece is playing it
the Irish composer John Field invented the nocturne, so a nocturne may be a Field

explanation.surface: Asking what musical pitch suits a performance of a nocturne.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Pitch' looks musical, but it is a sports ground; the question mark flags the composer naming his work.
explanation.definitionFit: A playing field is a grassy area marked out for sports, which is what a pitch is.

clue.text: Flower-girl with hot temper

parts.note: Iris is both a flower and a girl's name
H is the abbreviation for hot, as on taps

explanation.surface: A girl selling flowers who has a fiery temper.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Hot temper' looks like one phrase; 'temper' alone is the definition, from the idiom 'get one's Irish up'.
explanation.definitionFit: Irish is an informal, dated word for anger or temper, as in getting someone's Irish up.

clue.text: Life? That's about right

indicators.note: about means around, so one piece wraps round the other

parts.note: 'That' points back to the life just named, and bio is short for biography, a life story
R is the abbreviation for right

explanation.surface: Someone muses on existence and concludes it is roughly correct.
explanation.walkthrough: BIO goes around R to give BRIO.
explanation.definitionFit: Brio is vigour and vivacity, the sense of life in 'full of life'.

clue.text: HE has English in for wine

indicators.note: to have something is to hold it, so one piece is held inside

parts.note: HE is high explosive, and TNT is a high explosive
E is the abbreviation for English

explanation.surface: Someone stocks up on English bottles for the cellar.
explanation.walkthrough: E goes inside TNT to give TENT. 'HE' looks like a pronoun, but it stands for high explosive.
explanation.definitionFit: Tent is a deep red sweet wine from Spain, once common as a sacramental wine.

clue.text: Nine letters from here in return for one from abroad

indicators.note: a return goes back the way it came, so the letters are read backwards

parts.note: counting from the start of the alphabet, nine letters run A to I

explanation.surface: Swapping nine local letters in exchange for a single foreign one.
explanation.walkthrough: A TO I written backwards gives IOTA.
explanation.definitionFit: Iota is the Greek letter I, so it is a letter from a foreign alphabet, one from abroad.

clue.text: Relatively informative diagram of house

parts.note: surface reading: a fairly useful floor plan of a building
setter's reading: informative about relatives, and a house is a dynasty, as in the House of Windsor

explanation.surface: An architect's plan of a home that is moderately helpful.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Relatively' seems to mean 'fairly', but it means 'about relatives', and 'house' is a noble family line.
explanation.definitionFit: A family tree is a chart showing a lineage and how its relatives connect across generations.

clue.text: Attention given to Liberal peer

indicators.note: one thing given to another is attached to it, so the parts join up

parts.note: to give an ear is to pay attention
L is the abbreviation for Liberal

explanation.surface: A Liberal member of the House of Lords getting a hearing.
explanation.definitionFit: An earl is a British nobleman ranking above a viscount, and nobles are called peers.

clue.text: Lowest gain her doctor recorded — a stone

parts.note: to net is to gain, as in net a profit
taken as written
MO, medical officer, is a doctor on the official record
st is the abbreviation for stone, the unit of weight

explanation.surface: A doctor notes a patient's smallest weight gain: a single stone.
explanation.walkthrough: A stone is a British unit of body weight, 14 pounds.
explanation.definitionFit: Nethermost means farthest down, the most low of all, an old-fashioned word for lowest.
